title: Radial artery approach
view: Right volar wrist from above, palm up, wrist extended over a rolled towel: the operator's view. Forearm left, hand right, thumb side at the top.
teachingPoint: Puncture over the radial artery 1-2 cm proximal to the wrist crease, lateral to the FCR tendon - not at the crease, and not medial to FCR, where the median nerve runs.
claims: Right wrist, palm up, over a rolled towel. Forearm on the left, hand on the right, so the thumb (radial) side is at the top. Skin drawn see-through.
The radial artery runs lateral (here: above) to the flexor carpi radialis tendon; at the wrist it turns dorsally around the radial styloid (dashed = deep).
The median nerve runs medial to FCR, under palmaris longus. The ulnar artery lies radial to the FCU tendon.
The teal zone is the puncture target: over the radial artery, from 1 cm to 2 cm proximal to the wrist crease. The bracket spans crease to 2 cm, with a tick at 1 cm.
One wrist crease is drawn on purpose, so the distance has one reference.
Three labels: Radial artery, FCR tendon, Wrist crease.

geometry.why: radial artery is lateral (thumb side, above) to FCR
median nerve is medial to FCR
target zone is over the radial artery
target zone is not over FCR
target zone is not over the median nerve
target zone is proximal to the crease
target zone does not touch the crease
bracket spans crease to 2 cm (11 px/mm)
